t.1.158.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then those bulls among men, scorchers of their foes, set out with their mother at their head, travelling by level roads that led northward, as they had been instructed.
t.1.158.2: Journeying on through day and night, those tigers among men, the sons of Pāṇḍu, reached the sacred ford Somaśravāyaṇa on the Gaṅgā.
t.1.158.3: Raising a firebrand, the greatly renowned Dhanaṃjaya went there at their head, both to give light and to protect them.
t.1.158.5: He heard the sound of them as they approached the river, and, seized by that sound, the mighty one grew violently angry.
t.1.158.4: There, in the lovely, secluded waters of the Gaṅgā, the women were at play, and the jealous king of the Gandharvas had come there for sport in the water.
t.1.158.6: Seeing there the Pāṇḍavas, scorchers of foes, together with their mother, he twanged his terrible bow and spoke these words.
t.1.158.7: The dreadful twilight that reddens at the coming of the early night, they declare that span to be a muhūrta short by eighty truṭis.
t.1.158.9: Foolish men who, out of greed, go roaming about at those hours, we, together with the Rākṣasas, attack and seize.
t.1.158.8: This time is ordained for the Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas, who roam at will; the remaining part, the other, is held here to be the time when men may move about as they please.
t.1.158.10: Therefore people who know brahman censure all men who come to the water at night, even kings who stand at the head of their forces.
t.1.158.12: Know me to be the Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa, one who relies on his own strength. For I am proud and jealous, and a dear friend of Kubera.
t.1.158.11: Stay at a distance, do not come near me! Why do you not recognize me, who have come to the water of the Bhāgīrathī?
t.1.158.13: And this forest of mine is known as Aṅgāraparṇa; it lies along the Gaṅgā and the Vākā, a wondrous place where I dwell.
t.1.158.15: In the ocean, on the slopes of Himavat, and in this river, O fool, by night, by day, and at twilight, for whom has exclusive possession been ordained?
t.1.158.14: Neither corpses nor horned beasts, neither gods nor men approach this place; why then do you approach it?
t.1.158.17: This Gaṅgā, having issued of old from the golden peak of Himavant, reaches the waters of the ocean and becomes sevenfold.
t.1.158.16: We, endowed with strength, dare to assail you even at the forbidden hour; for it is powerless men who pay homage to you at the cruel hour.
t.1.158.18: And this pure Gaṅgā, having become single-streamed and coursing through the sky, once more among the gods, O Gandharva, attains the state of being the Alakanandā.
t.1.158.20: The river of the gods is unobstructed, auspicious, the bestower of heaven; how can you wish to block her? This is not the eternal law.
t.1.158.19: Likewise, O Gandharva, for the ancestors the Gaṅgā becomes the Vaitaraṇī, hard to cross for those of evil deeds, as Dvaipāyana said.
t.1.158.22: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that, Aṅgāraparṇa, enraged, bent his bow and loosed blazing arrows like venomous serpents.
t.1.158.21: How, at your mere word, should we not touch as we please the holy water of the Bhāgīrathī, which no one may bar and which is open to all?
t.1.158.23: Swiftly whirling a firebrand and an excellent shield, the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya warded off all of his arrows.
t.1.158.24: Arjuna said: This intimidation, O Gandharva, is not employed against those who know the weapons; employed against those skilled in weapons, it dissolves away like foam.
t.1.158.25: O Gandharva, I regard all Gandharvas as surpassing humans; therefore I shall fight you with a divine weapon, not with illusion.
t.1.158.28: Having spoken thus, the enraged Pāṇḍava released at the Gandharva the blazing fiery weapon of Agni, and it burned up his chariot.
t.1.158.27: From Bharadvāja it passed to Agniveśya, and from Agniveśya to my teacher; and he, Droṇa, the best of brahmins, gave it to me.
t.1.158.26: Long ago, O Gandharva, Bṛhaspati, the son of Śatakratu's guru, gave this fiery weapon to Bharadvāja, so it is said.
t.1.158.30: Dhanaṃjaya seized him by his garlanded locks of hair, and then he dragged him, senseless from the impact of the weapon, toward his brothers.
t.1.158.31: His wife, Kumbhīnasī by name, seeking refuge, approached Yudhiṣṭhira, desiring protection for her husband.
t.1.158.29: But that mighty Gandharva, bereft of his chariot, tossed about, stupefied by the blazing power of the weapon, and falling headlong, he seized.
t.1.158.32: Protect me, great king, and release this husband of mine, O lord; I am a Gandharvī named Kumbhīnasī, and I have come to you for refuge.
t.1.158.33: Who like you would slay an enemy who has been conquered in battle, who is bereft of glory, who has a woman for his protector and has no valor left? Release him, O slayer of foes.
t.1.158.34: Come now, accept this and go, Gandharva, do not grieve; today Yudhiṣṭhira, king of the Kurus, grants you freedom from fear.
t.1.158.35: I am defeated; I give up my former name and the state of being Aṅgāraparṇa. From today I shall boast neither of my strength nor of my name in any assembly of men.
t.1.158.37: This splendid, excellent chariot of mine has been burned by the fire of your weapon; and so I, who was Citraratha, have become by name Dagdharatha.
t.1.158.36: Well indeed have I won this gain, I who wished to fight with Gandharva magic against this bearer of divine weapons, superior in the vigor of youth.
t.1.158.39: For he who, having overpowered an enemy by force and conquered him, unites with life that foe who has come seeking refuge, what good fortune does he not deserve?
t.1.158.38: This knowledge was gathered by me here long ago through austerity; today I shall offer it to the great-souled one, in return for the gift of my life.
t.1.158.40: This knowledge is called Cakṣuṣī, the Two Eyes; Manu gave it to Soma, he gave it to Viśvāvasu, and Viśvāvasu gave it to me.
t.1.158.42: Whatever in the three worlds one should wish to see with the eye, that one may see; and in whatever form one should wish to see it, in that very form one is able to see it.
t.1.158.41: This knowledge, bestowed by a teacher, perishes when it falls to a coward. I have told you its origin; now learn from me its power.
t.1.158.43: One who has stood in the same posture for six months may obtain this knowledge. I myself shall pass this knowledge on to you once the vow has been fulfilled.
t.1.158.44: For by this knowledge, O king, we are set above men and are no different from the gods, moving about by its power.
t.1.158.47: Long ago the thunderbolt of the great Indra was fashioned for the slaying of Vṛtra; on Vṛtra's head it shattered tenfold, indeed a hundredfold.
t.1.158.45: O best of men, I will give your five brothers a hundred horses each, born in the land of the gandharvas, to each one separately.
t.1.158.46: These are the mounts of the gods and Gandharvas, divinely fragrant and swift as thought; though they grow worn and wasted again and again, they never fall off in speed.
t.1.158.48: Then the portion of the vajra, divided into shares by the gods, is worshipped; whatever instrument of accomplishment there is in the world is known as the body of the vajra.
t.1.158.49: The brahmin should be one whose hand is his thunderbolt; the kṣatra is known as having the chariot for its thunderbolt; the vaiśyas have giving as their thunderbolt, and the youngest have work as their thunderbolt.
t.1.158.51: These horses born of the gandharvas, taking whatever color they wish and running at whatever speed they wish, appearing whenever they are desired, will fulfill your every wish.
t.1.158.50: The thunderbolt of the kṣatra is the horse; horses are held to be inviolable. The mare is a part of the chariot that rests with the charioteer, and charioteers are those who are esteemed among horses.
t.1.158.52: Whether it is given out of goodwill or because your life is in danger, be it knowledge, wealth, or learning, I do not desire it, O Gandharva.
t.1.158.53: An alliance is indeed seen in assemblies to bring about affection. Pleased by your gift of my life, I give you this knowledge.
t.1.158.54: For I shall receive from you the supreme Āgneya weapon, and likewise let there be friendship between us for a long time, O Bībhatsu, bull among the Bharatas.
t.1.158.55: In exchange for the weapon I choose the horses from you; let the bond between us two be everlasting. Friend gandharva, tell me what would dispel the fear of you gandharvas.
